units.source_text: 与大诗人但丁的《神曲》和瑞典的大心灵学家斯威登堡的《天堂与地狱》相比，莱蒙特的灵界通讯只是像婴儿的牙牙学语。

en.t: Compared with the great poet Dante's Divine Comedy and the Swedish spiritual thinker Swedenborg's Heaven and Hell, Reymont's communications from the spirit world are only like the babbling of an infant.

units.source_text: 正因为这样，它才能像真正的童话故事，令人发出微笑。

en.t: Precisely because of this, they can seem like true fairy tales and bring a smile to one's face.

units.source_text: 另外，比起这一页冗长的像真事一般的记录来，我更喜欢那充满童话故事的篇章。

en.t: Besides, more than this page of long, seemingly factual records, I prefer those passages filled with fairy tales.

units.source_text: 就说洛茨吧，他也不相信巫师所说的那个世界的情况是真实的，只是同已故的儿子谈了许多许多，才证明灵魂是不灭的。

en.t: Take Lotz, for example: he too did not believe that the world described by the medium was real; only after speaking at great length with his dead son did he prove that the soul is immortal.

units.source_text: 由于欧洲大战，几十万母亲和恋人失去了自己心爱的人。

en.t: Because of the European war, hundreds of thousands of mothers and lovers lost the people they loved.

units.source_text: 这本书就是献给这些人的。

en.t: This book is dedicated precisely to those people.

units.source_text: 说实在的，莱蒙特为此现实地阐述了灵魂的永生，在我读过的无数的灵界通讯中，没有哪篇是比得上它的。

en.t: To tell the truth, Reymont set out the immortality of the soul in a realistic way for this purpose, and among the countless communications from the spirit world that I have read, none can compare with it.

units.source_text: 我跟你永别了，我必须从这本书中得到慰藉。

en.t: I have parted from you forever, and I must find consolation in this book.

units.source_text: 可是，我却在其中寻找一两个童话故事，可能这是件很不对头的事情。

en.t: Yet I am searching in it for one or two fairy tales, and perhaps that is a very misguided thing to do.
